messages:
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT ALERT 1768600000 - high paging, KV cache growth detected in us-west-2 :rotating_light:
Marta Ruiz: seeing sustained eviction rate spike + OOMs on rtx-pool-3, dashboards show KV allocated tokens doubling per minute :grimacing:
Kevin Zhang: aws metrics + flamegraphs?
Evan Patel: copying key panels — cache_entries, avg_kv_bytes, eviction_rate, contin_batch_size, tail_latency. avg_kv_bytes jumped from ~1.6MB -> 12MB per request window in 4m
Jun Ho: that looks like a batch multiplier runaway, maybe continuous batching config error from last rollout (batch.multiplier=auto->8 change)
Lia Gomez: customer impact: a few long-tail customers on Dedicated reported 5xxs and high latency. CS flagged 2 enterprise seats at 9:12.
Marta Ruiz: confirmed correlation with the 02:45 deploy that adjusted batch heuristics and introduced an experimental kernel selector for int8/awq
Kevin Zhang: hypothesis: AWQ/int8 kernel chose a path that expands KV representation (padding/packed-kv change) + larger batches amplified memory footprint -> snowballing allocations
Evan Patel: can we throttle batching or revert kernel selector quickly?
Jun Ho: I can patch config to cap batch.multiplier=2 and enable kv-eviction-throttle=on. Will do quick patch via control plane
Marta Ruiz: do it. Also add an emergency eviction cap per-model to prevent global cascade.
Ops Bot: running command: `redwoodctl config set --scope=global batch.multiplier=2 --reason "emergency kv snowball mitigation"`
Ops Bot: config applied to us-west-2; propagating to other regions (may take ~30s)
Evan Patel: rolling kernel selector back to safe path for int8 (force fp16 fallback) for models showing >5MB per-request KV
Jun Ho: command: `redwoodctl rollout kernelset --target=int8 --policy=fallback-fp16 --filter "kv_avg_bytes>5242880"`
Kevin Zhang: logs show eviction_rate stabilizing but tail latency still high, continuing to flush older KV entries.
Marta Ruiz: open runbook step: if eviction doesn't stabilize within 5m, scale dedicated pool by +2 nodes to reduce pressure.
Lia Gomez: I've told CS to message impacted customers: "We're investigating a KV cache-related latency issue; mitigation in progress, will update in 15m."
Evan Patel: metrics 2 minutes after patch: avg_kv_bytes falling from 12MB -> 3.2MB, eviction_rate down 70% :thumbsup:
Jun Ho: still seeing some paging for awq-backed models; kernel fallback taking time on warm instances -> plan B: temporarily disable awq kernel auto-select in runtime config
Marta Ruiz: agree. Put a quick toggle: `runtime.config.set awq_auto_select=false --region us-west-2`
Ops Bot: toggle applied. Notice: instances will reinitialize kernels on next model load (some short additional latency expected)
Kevin Zhang: flip done. Oncall note: recording this as a partial rollback + config caps.
Evan Patel: confirm runbook actions performed: capped batch multiplier, enabled eviction throttle, forced int8->fp16 fallback for heavy models, disabled awq_auto_select
Marta Ruiz: monitoring. Also need a postmortem stub and tentative severity P2 since some customers saw degraded service but no complete outages
Jun Ho: creating ticket INC-20260315-017 in tracker and adding runbook entries 
Jun Ho: ticket link: https://tracker.redwood.ai/INC-20260315-017 (placeholder)
Lia Gomez: CS notif updated: customers notified at 9:22 PT, next update at 9:37 PT
Marta Ruiz: handing off to second oncall for monitoring and postmortem: @Kevin Zhang please take main handoff, I'll be offline in 10m
Kevin Zhang: taking handoff. Summary for next oncall: KV snowball caused by batch.multiplier change + awq kernel path -> mitigations applied: batch cap, eviction throttle, kernel fallback, awq auto-select disabled. Watch avg_kv_bytes, eviction_rate, burst_paging, tail_latency.
Oncall Bot: Handoff recorded. Next handoff due in 4h.
Kevin Zhang: next steps for postmortem: 1) reproduce locally with traffic sim (batch multiplier 8 + awq kernel) 2) quantify KV size diff between kernels 3) add safety checks to rollout pipeline to block batch multiplier >4 without canary 4) add telemetry for per-kernel kv_bytes
Evan Patel: I'll start the kernel diff measurement (dump kv serialization sizes for sample sequences)
Marta Ruiz: thanks team. If we see reoccurrence, escalate to infra for emergency capacity scale or hotpatch runtime.
Lia Gomez: adding customer notes to ticket and CC'ing affected accounts
Jun Ho: arch note: long-term fix might be to bound per-request kv footprint in runtime and reject requests that exceed a threshold with a graceful error to avoid cross-tenant impact
Kevin Zhang: ack. Leaving monitoring alerts to fire on avg_kv_bytes > 6MB or paging_rps > 20.
Evan Patel: metrics look stable at 9:30 PT, continuing to observe for 30m then start postmortem draft
Marta Ruiz: thanks all. Closing incident thread once postmortem created and CS confirmed customer communications.
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT UPDATED - status: mitigated, severity: P2, responders: Marta Ruiz, Kevin Zhang, Jun Ho, Evan Patel, Lia Gomez
_meta: generated: production incident kv caching + batching regression (unique wording: 'snowball')
